review_state: factory C1 position and lower positive end corroborated by owner can; numbered pad and net identity remain open

assembly.observation: The exact .009 assembly draws C1 vertically immediately right of R3 and left of D13/D105, with a + sign beside its lower lead.

owner.observation: A fitted vertical metal can occupies the same R3/D13/D105 neighborhood. Its case shows a + marking near the lower bent lead, matching the assembly polarity. The opposite upper lead is separately visible. The can's capacity and voltage text cannot be read securely from this face.

source.observation: Exact .009 sheet 1 assigns C1=47,0 to the reset RC network; this source value does not establish the fitted can's measured capacitance or physical pad nets.

replica_footprint_check.observation: The source PCB currently places C1 as a 2 mm pitch radial electrolytic. The photographed metal can has one lead leaving each opposite end and mounted on a longer vertical span. The current footprint cannot be accepted as a traced copy of those owner holes.
replica_footprint_check.decision: Hold C1 mechanical sourcing and footprint selection until both owner drill centres are registered and a matching axial part or faithful mounting option is selected.

decision: Use the assembly-to-owner position and polarity match to identify the fitted can as the leading C1 body. Preserve the lower-positive physical orientation as photo evidence, but do not number its pads or connect the nearby R36 trace from proximity alone.
next_inspection: Power off: confirm each C1 lead's same-hole solder counterpart, lower marked-positive lead to the source-positive reset node, and upper lead to the other reset RC node. Measure the physical hole spacing before replacing the provisional radial footprint. Check the apparent R36-lower-to-can route separately across the white-wire occlusion.
